authored_scope: Supported: comb mazes of full-span parallel blue walls (thickness 1-2 when sampled, any in explicit mode) with top, bottom, middle or double-ended openings. Interior lanes are 1 wide and outer lanes 1-2 wide. Red cells sit in the outermost lanes. Optional dead-end lane caps act as distractors, and the whole frame can be transposed. Height is 3..30, width is at most 30, and there are 1..14 walls. Sizes above 10x10 and more than 4 walls are synthetic extensions of the same corridor mechanism. Deliberately not supported: free-form or branching mazes, wide interior lanes, red cells in interior lanes, scenes with tied shortest paths, and flips other than transposition (top/bottom opening sampling covers reflections in practice).
authored_constraints: Exactly two 2-cells, both in the outer lanes and both on 0 cells before placement.
The 1-D crossing-row DP has exactly one optimal choice, so the grid shortest path is unique.
Interior lanes are exactly 1 wide. A wide-outer-lane endpoint is on the inner column or level with its crossing row.
Each wall has at least one open row and at least one closed row.
Lane blocks never intersect the drawn path. They only remove cells, so the path stays the unique shortest one.
Total width is at most 30 and height is 3..30. The output differs from the input only by 0->4, and at least one cell changes.
Integer controls must be genuine ints. bool, float and malformed structures raise ValueError.
